raw_transcript:
Right. Lab notes, Tuesday, 6:40 pm. Um. Today was, today was mostly the brownout reset on the Heron pump controller board, rev C. So for context, when the pump motor starts, the board sometimes resets, and we see it maybe one in twenty starts. Kaito Brann from hardware thinks it's the 3.3 volt rail dipping, and I, I kind of thought it was a watchdog timeout in the motor init code. Turns out, well, partly both, I think.

So first thing this morning I put the scope on the 3.3 V rail, triggered on the motor enable GPIO. Dip goes down to 2.71 volts for about 180 microseconds. Wait, no, it was 2.91 volts, I'm reading my notebook wrong, 2.91. The brownout threshold on the MCU is configured at 2.8 volts, so, so 2.91 shouldn't trip BOR on its own. That kind of killed Kaito's theory, at least the simple version of it.

Then I went to the reset cause register. The RCC CSR flags, after a bad start, show the independent watchdog flag, IWDG, not the brownout flag. So it's the watchdog. The IWDG timeout is set to 250 milliseconds and the motor init routine does this, um, this blocking I2C read from the current sense chip, the INA-something, the INA229 I think, no it's the INA219, okay, and if the bus gets noisy during the inrush, the I2C transaction hangs and retries, and the retries add up past 250 ms. I saw one trace with the init taking 340 milliseconds. So the rail dip isn't resetting the chip directly, it's corrupting the I2C bus and then the watchdog fires. That's my current theory, I'd say 70 percent confident.

Uh, quick rant, the bench power supply on station 2 has the display that flickers and I spent like fifteen minutes thinking my readings were wrong. Someone needs to replace that. Probably me.

Okay. What I changed: I added a timeout of 5 milliseconds per I2C transaction, so the driver gives up instead of retrying forever, and I moved the watchdog kick into the retry loop. Wait, actually, no, I did not move the watchdog kick, I talked about it with Ruth Adeyemi, she's the firmware lead, and she said absolutely not, don't feed the watchdog inside a retry loop, that hides real hangs. Which, yeah, fair. So only the I2C timeout change went in. With that, I did 200 motor starts on the bench with the test jig, and got zero resets. Before the change it was 11 resets in 200 starts. So, that's promising, but it's one board, at room temperature, and Ruth wants it repeated on three boards and in the thermal chamber at minus 10 C before we believe it.

Also, I should say, Kaito is still going to add a bigger bulk capacitor, 100 microfarad, on the motor supply in rev D, because even if it's not causing resets the dip on the I2C lines is ugly. That's his change, not mine, and it's not built yet.

The branch is fix/i2c-timeout, I pushed it but didn't open the merge request yet, because I want to clean up the logging. Firmware version on the bench was 2.4.1.

Plans. Thermal chamber is booked for Thursday at 10, I think 10, let me check, yes 10 am. The release candidate cut is next Friday the 16th, so if this is going in, it needs to be merged by then. I have not tested on the other two boards yet because, um, one of them, board serial 0047, has a cracked connector and I'm waiting on a spare.

That's it. Going home.

Oh and, um, I forgot, Ruth also asked me to check the stack high-water mark on the motor task, since I added the timeout logic. It was, uh, 312 bytes free out of 1024, so that's fine, no change needed there. And, and the flash usage went up by 96 bytes. Not a concern. I also, I want to note this so I don't forget, the scope probe on channel 3 is the one with the bent ground spring, don't use it, it adds ringing that looks like a real signal. Lost half an hour to that last week.

The IWDG timeout is set to 250 milliseconds, and the motor init routine does a blocking I2C read from the current sense chip, the INA219. If the bus gets noisy during the inrush, the I2C transaction hangs and retries, and the retries add up past 250 ms. I saw one trace with the init taking 340 milliseconds. So the rail dip isn't resetting the chip directly; it corrupts the I2C bus and then the watchdog fires. That's my current theory, about 70 percent confident.

The bench power supply on station 2 has a flickering display, and I spent fifteen minutes thinking my readings were wrong. Someone needs to replace it.

I did not move the watchdog kick into the retry loop; I discussed it with Ruth Adeyemi, the firmware lead, and she said not to feed the watchdog inside a retry loop because that hides real hangs. So only the I2C timeout change went in. With that, I did 200 motor starts on the bench with the test jig and got zero resets. Before the change it was 11 resets in 200 starts.
